extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists and editorial staff worldwide
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive set of ethical, editorial and procedural standards that govern how Reuters journalists gather, produce and publish news across text, picture, TV and online platforms. Covers accuracy, sourcing, independence, conflicts, use of images, AI, and staff conduct inside and outside the newsroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Trust Principles in all activities related to Reuters News.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Principles underpin independence, accuracy and freedom from bias and should guide all editorial and journalistic decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold accuracy sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is at the heart of what we do; it is our job to get it first but above all to get it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and balance always take precedence over speed. Think how you would withstand a challenge or a denial before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek fair comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek fair comment by giving subjects the opportunity to put their side and ensuring allegations are not portrayed as fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to be scrupulously fair and balanced; talk to sources on all sides of a deal, dispute, negotiation or conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct errors transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters is transparent about errors and rectifies them promptly, clearly and comprehensively whether in a story, caption, graphic or script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should be visible, timely and comprehensive; complaints that cannot be immediately investigated must be acknowledged at once and followed up quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for balance and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for balance and freedom from bias; park nationality and politics at the door and avoid taking sides in conflicts or disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid language that implies editorial judgment (e.g., 'fail', 'refute'); provide appropriate space to different parties based on newsworthiness, not parity alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose potential or actual conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose potential or actual conflicts of interest to a manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any activity or relationship could give rise to a perception of bias, raise it with your manager; Reuters may require reassignment where perceptions persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unattributed opinion in news
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid injecting unattributed opinion in a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion belongs in clearly labelled opinion pieces or columns; news must be fact-based and neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fabricate or plagiarise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fabricate information or plagiarise others’ work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication or plagiarism may lead to disciplinary measures including dismissal; attribute clearly and honestly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter still images or video beyond normal editorial preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not alter still images or video footage beyond the methods normally used to prepare content for editorial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual journalism must reflect reality; actions that add to or detract from reality may constitute fabrication and cause serious reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay for information or accept a bribe or trade on privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pay for information, accept a bribe, or trade on privileged (material non-public) information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conduct is a grave breach of ethics and may be grounds for immediate dismissal and legal liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy — prioritize getting it right over speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy always comes first; it is better to be late than wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check information, weigh unnamed sources’ track record and motive, and ensure you can defend the story to sources and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections — rectify promptly and transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent and prompt when rectifying errors in any published or broadcast material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should state what was wrong and what has been changed; handle at a senior level when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing — use named sources where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: A named source is preferable to an unnamed source because they are accountable for the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press sources to go on the record; when using unnamed sources, weigh track record, position and motive; document interviews and, where allowed, record them; special authorisation required for single-source stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing honesty — do not mislead about sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Never deliberately mislead in sourcing, quote a source inconsistently on and off the record, or claim multiple sources when there is only one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about what you don’t know and give context and detail about sources to authenticate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-source stories — require special authorisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish news from a single, anonymous source only in exceptional cases with special authorisation and when the source is trusted and credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-source market-moving stories are subject to an approval procedure; the newsroom bears full responsibility for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting sources — confidentiality is paramount but may be disclosed to supervisors
rubrics_metrics.description: A source’s compact is with Reuters; reporters are expected to disclose sources to supervisors on legitimate editorial grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidentiality vigorously between reporter and supervisor; disclosure may be required internally to address legal or editorial issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check and attempt to disprove initiative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When doing initiative reporting, try to disprove as well as prove your story; cross-check wherever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two or more corroborating sources are better than one; use common sense and follow up if something sounds wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes — preserve meaning and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes are sacrosanct and must not be altered except to delete redundant words or clauses without changing sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid selective quoting that skews balance; provide context, body language where relevant; correct minor grammar only, not whole phrasing; consult seniors when in doubt; translate idiomatically while preserving tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflecting reality — avoid hype and sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories and images must reflect reality and must not be hyped or sensationalised in ways that mislead or harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think how word choices (e.g., 'flood', 'surge') change perceptions; visual decisions that misrepresent reality may be fabrication and are disciplinable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datelines and bylines — must accurately reflect presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylines should indicate the writer was at the dateline; use datelines only where Reuters staff or freelancers were present or contributing on the ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contributors in an additional-reporting line with name and location; do not imply on-the-ground presence when absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution — identify the source of material clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly attribute material that is not produced by Reuters so customers can assess reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sources specifically (e.g., 'Greenpeace Video' or 'U.S. Army Photo'); merely saying 'handout' is insufficient and could be perceived as plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rumours — differentiate fact from rumour
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to report facts, not rumours, while explaining when rumours affect markets and attempting to verify or knock them down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptional circumstances may permit moving before full verification if a market is moving violently; otherwise verify rumors and track origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic images and obscenities — publish only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic material should not be published gratuitously; there must be a valid news reason and senior-editor decision is usually required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider if material is necessary for understanding reality; precede packaged videos with 'Warning: Graphic Content'; be mindful of different market thresholds (broadcast vs online consumer use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence — avoid conflicts and preserve impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence is essential; avoid activities or relationships that could create actual or perceived conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a potential conflict arises, raise it with your manager; independence stems from Trust Principles and company structures ensuring editorial separation from commercial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal investments — do not let investments influence work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow personal or immediate-family investments to influence reporting; avoid reporting on entities you or family have interests in or trading on that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct regarding personal investments and nonpublic information; violations are subject to disciplinary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring financial interests — avoid suspicion of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure no circumstances exist that could give rise to suspicion of bias due to financial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and clear potential conflicts per company code; where doubtful, consult Ethics and Standards or legal counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work outside Reuters — seek prior permission for paid outside work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not engage in paid outside work without manager approval; permission is routinely granted if activities do not affect Reuters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include books, articles, speaking; NewsGuild members in the U.S. may have different second-job rules depending on competition concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking back with sources — do not let sources vet copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit stories, scripts or images to sources for vetting before publication; checking back for verification is permissible but must not allow material changes by sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist requests to approve quotes; if approval is given, do not agree to material changes; notify seniors when coerced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and entertainment — decline significant gifts and junkets
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept payments, gifts or benefits from news sources beyond nominal cultural tokens; refuse gifts of more than nominal value and consult manager if unsure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitality that is newsworthy and reasonable may be accepted; do not accept 'junkets' or hospitality with little news value; surrender gifts of value to a manager if unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and accommodation from sources — normally pay your own way
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should normally pay their own travel and make arrangements; accept free travel only with manager approval when necessary for access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission may be given in exceptional cases (remote famine, war zone) and reimbursement to the offering entity is preferable where practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bribes and inducements — never take or offer payment for stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Under no circumstances should staff take or offer payment for news stories; this undermines independence and is grounds for dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid entertainment beyond normal hospitality; consult company anti-bribery policies and be aware of local restrictions for government officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering competitions and receiving awards — obtain approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may submit Reuters work to reputable journalism contests with manager approval; do not submit primarily to win awards or alter work for that purpose beyond competition rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions to contests not judged by journalists require higher-level approvals; unsolicited awards and jury invitations need approval before acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity — adhere to the highest ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Act with personal integrity, respect local laws and cultures, and accept responsibilities inherent to being a Reuters journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional conduct at all times; integrity helps preserve Reuters’ reputation in all dealings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying ourselves as journalists — do not obtain news by deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not misrepresent yourself; do not pass yourself off as something other than a journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some cases assumptions may be left to persist in the interest of newsgathering; if directly questioned, identify as Reuters journalist; apply Code of Conduct and managerial guidance when unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting from the Internet — apply the same standards online
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the same principles of sourcing, identification and verification to online reporting as to other forms of newsgathering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take the same precautions online; do not use material that cannot be sourced and verified; treat online information as potentially interfered with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading — do not trade on material non-public information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not buy or sell securities or tip others while in possession of material non-public information obtained in the course of Reuters employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material information includes mergers, bankruptcies, forecasts, management changes, etc.; assume information from Reuters is non-public until widely disclosed and absorbed by markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with sources — cultivate sources professionally and maintain detachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Be polite and fair; cultivate sources while maintaining professional detachment so relationships do not create bias or perception of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive leisure time with a source; disclose romantic or family attachments that could affect coverage; do not report on or quote family members to avoid perception of favouritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with customers — maintain separation of editorial and commercial functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat customers professionally but avoid negotiating sales contracts or allowing commercial relationships to influence editorial coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to the line that separates editorial and commercial functions; do not trade editorial favours for commercial advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with people in stories — show sensitivity and avoid harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat victims with sensitivity, avoid needless pain or offence, seek clear facts, avoid sensationalism, and be alert to spin and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should show integrity, impartiality, persistence, accountability and humility and be prepared to defend stories to critics and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with competitors — obtain information properly and acknowledge exclusives
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain information about competitors lawfully; attribute competitors' exclusive reporting when used and avoid improper deals or sharing of editorial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperate with competitors in safety or when pooling information is in the public interest; do not 'do deals' that compromise independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with complaints — investigate promptly and escalate appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints about accuracy, balance or ethics must be investigated promptly and acknowledged if immediate investigation is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle complaints at a senior level and escalate to Ethics and Standards leads when in doubt; maintain constructive attitude and treat complaints as feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with the authorities — refer requests for material to senior editors/legal
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests from police, tribunals or lawyers for published or unpublished Reuters content should be referred to a senior editor and editorial legal team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish published from unpublished material; do not voluntarily hand over unpublished material and consider lawful challenges to subpoenas to protect staff safety and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with each other — foster teamwork and a respectful workplace
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint planning and cooperation across disciplines is required; staff should be able to raise standards concerns without fear of recrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat colleagues with dignity and respect; promote an environment free from harassment and ensure issues are resolved confidentially and without reprisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting incidents internally — report serious incidents promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers and staff must report incidents involving harm, hoaxes, improper behaviour or problems with stories/images to keep senior officials informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reporting helps spot trends and prevent reputational damage; non-managerial staff must report to supervisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life outside Reuters — avoid confusion between professional and private activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure private opinions or activities do not appear to represent Reuters; be cautious when using company systems for personal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid expressions of political opinion or investment advice on company systems; use private email for potentially sensitive personal correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from bias — maintain neutrality and avoid taking sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain neutrality, welcome diversity in the newsroom, and park personal politics and nationality when reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for scrupulous fairness; be wary of bias in word choice and framing; ensure subjects can put their side where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take no side, tell all sides — reflect all relevant sides in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Never identify with any side in an issue; reflect all sides so reporting is balanced and defensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal space is not always required; allocate space based on news value; always ask 'What do I know?' and 'What do I need to know?'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion and Analysis — clearly label viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish fact-based news from clearly labeled opinion pieces; journalists must not express personal opinions in news stories or in voiced video/scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns and point-of-view pieces must be clearly labelled and disclaim that they do not represent Reuters; authors should ground opinions in expertise and avoid provocation or personal attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminatory language and stereotypes — avoid inappropriate references
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inappropriate references to gender, ethnicity, religion, appearance, age and sexual orientation and be sensitive to unconscious stereotyping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral language, avoid gratuitous references to appearance, prefer inclusive plurals (e.g., 'executives' rather than gendered titles), and proceed cautiously when challenging stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment advice — do not give personal investment views
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not express personal views on the merits of specific investments; value judgments must be sourced to a named third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters reports news and must not give investment advice; local laws may prohibit doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Thomson Reuters — take extreme care to avoid bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Take extreme care when reporting on Thomson Reuters and its affiliates to avoid perceived bias; stories must be seen before publication by senior editors and the Global Editor for Ethics and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories must include comment from a company spokesman and be limited to market-moving or significant-interest items; identify Thomson Reuters entities explicitly when quoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political and Community Activity — avoid public displays of partisan support
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not give support to political parties or identify Reuters with any partisan cause; staff should be sensitive that outside political activities may create perceptions of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common sense and consult managers when in doubt; in some cases Reuters may require reassignment to avoid perceived conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Opportunity in the Newsroom — fair employment practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat employees fairly regardless of gender, ethnicity, religion, age, disability, marital or parental status or sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for hiring, training and promotion should be based on relevant skills and in accordance with local laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity in the Newsroom — welcome and use diverse perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace diversity of thought, culture, identity and background to enrich journalism and debate about the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity should inform coverage and newsroom decision-making to produce better journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media interviews and speaking engagements — obtain approval and stick to facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews must be approved in advance by a manager and communications team; correspondents should not give personal opinions and should focus on Reuters-reported facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer credible outlets; payment should not be sought or accepted; interviews for Reuters services take precedence; consult communications before speaking to outside media about conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conferences — approval required and limits on participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in conferences requires editorial approval; journalists should not moderate or participate in panels where paid participation or product promotion is primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists can moderate only if Reuters controls content; avoid events where panelists paid to participate or where primary aim is product launch; do not accept payment or travel/lodging from hosts except under strict approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI — maintain editorial accountability and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace AI opportunities but maintain editorial accountability for all output and be transparent about GenAI use; do not use generative AI to create or enhance imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never trust unverified facts from AI; independently verify all facts, sources and claims generated by AI; do not upload Reuters or partner content to non-approved external tools; approved tools may assist with non-visual tasks (e.g., shotlists, captions).
